On Indian roads, which side of the road should you normally drive on?
questions.explanation: India drives on the left. Keep to the left and let faster traffic pass on your right.

questions.question: From which side should you normally overtake another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Overtake from the right. You may pass on the left only when the vehicle ahead has signalled a right turn and moved to turn.

questions.question: The vehicle ahead has signalled a right turn and moved to the centre. How may you pass it?
wrong: By sounding the horn and pushing past
questions.explanation: When a vehicle is turning right, you may pass it on the left if the way is clear.

questions.question: When is overtaking not allowed?
questions.correct: When the road ahead is not clearly visible
wrong: When the vehicle ahead signals you to pass
On a wide highway with no traffic
questions.explanation: Do not overtake at bends, hill tops, junctions, pedestrian crossings or whenever you cannot see the road ahead clearly.

questions.question: Another vehicle is overtaking you. What should you do?
questions.correct: Keep left and do not speed up
wrong: Speed up so it cannot pass
questions.explanation: Help the overtaking vehicle pass safely. Never increase your speed while being overtaken.

questions.question: A pedestrian is waiting to cross at a zebra crossing. What should you do?
questions.correct: Slow down and stop to let them cross
wrong: Speed up to pass before they step out
questions.explanation: Pedestrians on or waiting at a zebra crossing have the right of way.

questions.question: An ambulance or fire engine is coming with its siren on. What should you do?
questions.correct: Move to the side of the road and let it pass
wrong: Keep going at the same speed
Stop in the middle of the road
questions.explanation: Emergency vehicles have priority. Give way by pulling to the side.

questions.question: What does a steady red traffic light mean?
wrong: Go if the road is clear
questions.explanation: Stop behind the stop line and wait for green.

questions.question: What does a steady amber (yellow) traffic light mean?
questions.correct: Stop, unless you are too close to stop safely
wrong: Go, the light is about to turn green
questions.explanation: Amber warns that red is next. Stop if you safely can.

questions.question: What does a flashing amber traffic light mean?
questions.correct: Slow down and proceed with caution
wrong: The signal is broken, so stop
questions.explanation: A flashing amber light means go ahead carefully, watching for other traffic.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
questions.correct: Stop, then go when it is safe
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red like a stop sign.

questions.question: The traffic light is green but a traffic police officer signals you to stop. What do you do?
questions.correct: Obey the police officer and stop
wrong: Obey the green light and go
questions.explanation: Signals from a traffic police officer take priority over traffic lights.

questions.question: At a roundabout, which vehicles should you give way to?
questions.correct: Vehicles already in the roundabout, coming from your right
wrong: No one, if you are faster
questions.explanation: In India, traffic moves clockwise around a roundabout. Give way to vehicles coming from your right.

questions.question: At a junction with no signals or signs, whom should you give way to?
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled junction, give way to traffic on your right and to vehicles on the main road.

questions.question: You are entering a main road from a side road. What should you do?
questions.correct: Give way to traffic on the main road
wrong: Expect main road traffic to stop for you
questions.explanation: Traffic on the main road has priority.

questions.question: What does a continuous (solid) line in the centre of the road mean?
questions.correct: Do not cross it or overtake
questions.explanation: A solid centre line means no crossing or overtaking.

questions.question: What does a broken (dashed) white line in the centre of the road mean?
questions.correct: You may cross it to overtake when safe
questions.explanation: Broken lines may be crossed when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Where should you stop at a red light?
wrong: In the middle of the junction
questions.explanation: Never stop on the pedestrian crossing. Stop behind the stop line.

questions.question: Where is parking not allowed?
questions.correct: Near a road junction or bend
questions.explanation: Do not park near junctions, bends, hill tops, bus stops, pedestrian crossings, fire hydrants, or on a footpath.

questions.question: Is parking allowed on a footpath?
questions.explanation: Footpaths are for pedestrians. Parking on them is not allowed.

questions.question: Where should you not park your vehicle?
questions.correct: In front of a hospital entrance
questions.explanation: Never block hospital entrances, fire hydrants, bus stops or gates.

questions.question: Where is the use of the horn prohibited?
questions.explanation: Areas near hospitals, courts and schools are silence zones. Do not sound your horn there.

questions.question: When should the horn be used?
questions.correct: Only when necessary, to warn of danger
questions.explanation: Use the horn sparingly. Needless or continuous honking is not allowed.

questions.question: Are pressure horns or multi-tone horns allowed?
questions.explanation: Air pressure horns and multi-tone horns are not allowed on vehicles.

questions.question: How many people may ride on a motorcycle?
questions.correct: The rider and one pillion rider
wrong: The rider and two pillion riders
questions.explanation: A two-wheeler may carry only one pillion rider, seated properly behind the rider.

questions.question: What should you do at an unmanned railway level crossing?
questions.correct: Stop, look both ways, then cross when it is clear
questions.explanation: At an unmanned crossing, stop, check both directions for trains, and cross only when it is safe.

questions.question: The gate of a railway level crossing is closed. What should you do?
questions.correct: Stop and wait until it opens
questions.explanation: Never try to cross a closed level-crossing gate.

questions.question: You want to turn right. Where should your vehicle be?
questions.correct: Near the centre of the road
wrong: On the wrong side of the road
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move towards the centre of the road and signal.

questions.question: You want to turn left. Where should your vehicle be?
questions.correct: Close to the left side of the road
wrong: In the centre of the road
questions.explanation: Keep to the left before turning left.

questions.question: What does a driver extending the right arm straight out of the window mean?
questions.explanation: An arm held straight out to the right signals a right turn.

questions.question: A driver moves the right arm up and down, palm facing down. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Moving the arm up and down signals that the vehicle is slowing down.

questions.question: Is driving in reverse allowed on a one-way road?
questions.explanation: Do not reverse into or along a one-way road.

questions.question: On a one-way road, can you drive against the direction of traffic?
wrong: Yes, if it is a shortcut
questions.explanation: Driving against the flow on a one-way road is an offence and very dangerous.

questions.question: On a hill road, who should normally get the right of way?
questions.explanation: On narrow hill roads, give way to vehicles coming uphill, since restarting on a slope is harder.

questions.question: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for driving in India?
questions.explanation: Driving with more than 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood is an offence. The safest choice is not to drink at all.

questions.question: Is it allowed to use a hand-held mobile phone while driving?
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held phone while driving is an offence. Pull over safely if you must make a call.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a motorcycle?
questions.correct: Both the rider and the pillion rider
questions.explanation: Rider and pillion must wear a properly fastened helmet.

questions.question: Who should wear a seat belt in a car?
wrong: Only front seat passengers on highways
questions.explanation: Seat belts save lives. Everyone in the car should wear one.

questions.question: When driving at night and a vehicle comes from the front, what should you do with your headlights?
questions.explanation: High beam dazzles oncoming drivers. Dip your lights.

questions.question: How much distance should you keep from the vehicle in front?
questions.correct: Enough to stop safely if it brakes suddenly
wrong: No gap is needed in slow traffic
questions.explanation: Keep a safe gap, and increase it in rain, fog or at higher speed.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in thick fog?
questions.correct: Slow down and use dipped headlights or fog lamps
wrong: Drive fast to get out of the fog
Follow the vehicle ahead very closely
questions.explanation: High beam reflects off fog and reduces visibility. Slow down and use low beam or fog lamps.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a bend?
questions.explanation: Reduce speed before the bend and stay on your side.

questions.question: What are hazard warning lights used for?
questions.correct: To warn others that your vehicle is stopped and is a hazard
questions.explanation: Use hazard lights when your vehicle has broken down or is stopped in an unsafe place.

questions.question: Why are rear-view mirrors fitted?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often, especially before changing lanes, turning or slowing down.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?
questions.correct: Before changing lanes, turning or slowing down
questions.explanation: Mirror, signal, then manoeuvre.

questions.question: A school bus has stopped to let children get off. What should you do?
questions.correct: Slow down and be ready to stop
questions.explanation: Children may run across the road. Drive slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Near a school, how should you drive?
questions.correct: Slowly and carefully, watching for children
wrong: Fast, to clear the area quickly
Using the horn all the time
questions.explanation: School zones need extra care and low speed.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving causes many crashes. Take a break.

questions.question: The road is wet after rain. What should you do?
questions.correct: Drive slower and keep a bigger gap
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery and need longer stopping distances.

questions.question: Your brakes fail on a slope. What is the safest thing to do?
questions.correct: Change to a lower gear and use the hand brake gently
wrong: Switch off the engine and steer
questions.explanation: Lower gears use engine braking to slow you. Apply the hand brake gradually.

questions.question: You are involved in an accident and someone is injured. What should you do?
questions.correct: Get medical help for the injured and inform the police
wrong: Wait for the other driver to act
questions.explanation: The driver must help get the injured to medical care and report the accident to the police.

questions.question: Within how much time should a road accident be reported to the police?
questions.explanation: If not reported on the spot, an accident must be reported to the nearest police station within 24 hours.

questions.question: What is a "Good Samaritan" under Indian road law?
questions.correct: A bystander who helps an accident victim in good faith
questions.explanation: The law protects people who help road accident victims in good faith from harassment and liability.

questions.question: What is the all-in-one emergency number in India?
questions.explanation: Dial 112 for police, fire or ambulance help.

questions.question: Why should you not drive with worn-out tyres?
questions.correct: They can skid or burst, causing an accident
questions.explanation: Worn tyres have less grip, especially on wet roads.

questions.question: When should you use the indicator?
questions.explanation: Signal early so others know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Can a vehicle carry more passengers or load than it is permitted to?
wrong: Yes, if the driver is careful
questions.explanation: Overloading makes a vehicle unstable and is an offence.

questions.question: How long is a learner's licence valid?
questions.explanation: A learner's licence is valid for six months.

questions.question: After getting a learner's licence, when can you apply for a permanent driving licence?
questions.explanation: You can take the driving test for a permanent licence 30 days after the learner's licence is issued, and before it expires.

questions.question: What must a learner display on the vehicle?
questions.correct: An "L" sign on the front and back
questions.explanation: The letter L in red on a white background must be shown on the front and rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: A learner is driving a car. Who must sit beside them?
questions.correct: A person holding a valid driving licence for that vehicle
questions.explanation: A learner driving a car must have a licensed driver beside them who can take control.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to get a licence for a motorcycle with gears?
questions.explanation: You must be 18 for a licence for motorcycles with gear and for cars.

questions.question: At what age can you get a licence for a gearless two-wheeler up to 50 cc, with a parent's consent?
questions.explanation: At 16 you can get a licence for a gearless motorcycle with an engine up to 50 cc, with consent of a parent or guardian.

questions.question: Which documents must you carry while driving a private vehicle?
questions.correct: Driving licence, registration certificate, insurance and PUC certificate
questions.explanation: Carry your licence, RC, insurance certificate and Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate.

questions.question: Are digital documents in DigiLocker or mParivahan accepted?
questions.explanation: Documents in DigiLocker or mParivahan are accepted as valid by traffic police.

questions.question: Which insurance is compulsory for every motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: At least third-party insurance is required by law.

questions.question: What does PUC stand for?
questions.explanation: A PUC certificate shows your vehicle's emissions are within limits.

questions.question: How long is the registration of a new private car valid?
questions.explanation: Registration of a non-transport vehicle is valid for 15 years and can then be renewed.

questions.question: Can you drive a vehicle with an expired driving licence?
questions.explanation: Renew your licence before it expires.

questions.question: Can you lend your vehicle to someone without a driving licence?
wrong: Yes, if they are an adult
Yes, if they know how to drive
questions.explanation: The owner can be held responsible for letting an unlicensed person drive.

questions.question: Can a person under 18 drive a car on public roads?
questions.explanation: A licence to drive a car is issued only from age 18. Guardians or owners can be penalised if a minor drives.
